To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a deep learning-based matching approach is proposed for the registration of TerraSAR-X SAR data with PRISM optical satellite imagery; (2) the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art matching approaches in terms of accuracy, reliability, and robustness; (3) the proposed approach is used to improve the geo-localization performance of the PRISM images; (4) the improved geo-location accuracy is used to generate a geocoded PRISM time series; (5)

the proposed deep learning-based approach allows to: 1) derive accurate and reliable matching point pairs for SAR and optical image registration; 2) achieve an improved geo-localization of the optical image with respect to state of the art approaches.

a Siamese network is able to learn the spatial shifts between optical satellite images and SAR images with high accuracy, and that this approach is able to improve the geo-localization error of optical images with respect to SAR data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) the use of deep learning to improve the geo-localization precision and accuracy of optical images through SAR reference images, and (ii) the use of SAR data for the generation of matching points between optical and SAR images.
the development of a deep learning-based method for the geo-localizing of optical satellite images with respect to SAR reference data.
a new method for the geo-localized matching of SAR and optical satellite images, based on deep Siamese networks.
